claims: Evening / Afternoon Shift 1.15x - 1.25x and Night / Early Morning 1.15x - 1.3x (generic 'When Do Penalty Rates Apply?' table)
whys: The callout at line 179 on the same page says hospitality evening and night work is a flat cash amount, not a multiplier, and that guides printing 1.15x are wrong. The generic table prints 1.15x anyway. The table cells are locked, so the contradiction stays.
constants: HOSPITALITY_PENALTIES.eveningPerHour / nightPerHour and RETAIL_PENALTIES.eveningAfter6pm in lib/constants/hospitality-award.ts
reviewerNotes: I agree with the writer's fact questions. These are the generic table's 1.15x hospitality multipliers (they contradict the line 179 callout), the abolished 4-yearly award review and 'then renegotiated' at line 262, '12 months' for casual conversion and two old changes listed as FY2026-27 changes (lines 331-332), the 7.6-hour daily trigger at line 146, '5 key factors' versus s62(3) at line 310, and the unsourced population and threshold claims at lines 204, 246 and 319.

claims: Casual conversion pathway changes ... convert to permanent employment after 12 months (listed as a FY2026-27 change)
whys: This conflicts with line 304: the employee choice pathway has applied since 26 August 2024, after 6 months (12 months for a small business employer). It is also not a FY2026-27 change. Line 331 (Right to Disconnect, August 2024 and August 2025) is also listed as a FY2026-27 change but is older.
constants: hard-coded list item; should match the casual conversion text at line 304

claims: Overtime is triggered when a full-time employee exceeds 38 ordinary hours per week or 7.6 hours per day (for a 5-day week)
whys: 7.6 hours is the average day of a 38-hour week, not the award trigger. Awards set their own daily ordinary-hours limits, and the General Retail award allows ordinary shifts longer than 7.6 hours, so stating 7.6 hours as the daily trigger looks wrong.
constants: EMPLOYMENT.standardWeeklyHours plus award-specific daily ordinary hours (not in constants)

claims: The Fair Work Act ... requires consideration of 5 key factors to determine reasonableness
whys: Fair Work Act s62(3) lists about ten matters (a) to (j), not 5. The bullet list at lines 312-318 shows only five of them.
constants: hard-coded; source is Fair Work Act s62(3)

claims: most awards recognise 5 distinct penalty periods
whys: This is an unsourced count about 'most awards'. Hospitality uses flat cash amounts for evening and night work, not periods with multipliers.

claims: 30% marginal rate for $45,001 to $135,000, 2% Medicare levy, 1.25x Saturday and 1.5x Sunday (lines 238, 240, 247, 330, 334)
whys: The figures are correct for FY2026-27 but are typed into the text instead of coming from the tax and award constants, so they will drift at the next change.
constants: tax bracket and MEDICARE_LEVY constants in lib/constants/australian-tax.ts; RETAIL_PENALTIES.saturday/sunday

claims: Emergency service workers, healthcare professionals, and essential infrastructure employees face different reasonableness thresholds
whys: This is an unsourced claim. s62(3) weighs the nature of the role and the needs of the workplace, but it sets no separate thresholds for named groups.
